versions.changelog: v0.2.0: Add scripts/follow.py - tail -F equivalent for live log monitoring, log-aware. Streams new lines as they arrive with the same --pattern / --not-pattern / --level / --since filters as grep.py. Automatic log-rotation detection (inode change or file truncation triggers transparent reopen). --max-events N exits cleanly after N matched events (CI-friendly), --timeout SECONDS exits on inactivity, --json emits per-line JSON envelopes with extracted timestamp + level. Closes the only documented limitation from v0.1.x ('It does not tail/follow live log files').

v0.1.1 bug-fix release. Timestamp parser now accepts date-only values for grep.py --since / --until: 2026-05-09, 2026/05/09, 09/05/2026, and Y-m-d H:M (minute precision). Previously only full ISO 8601 timestamps worked, so users trying --since 2026-05-09 got a 'could not parse' error. No CLI changes.

v0.1.0 initial release. Third skill in the 'clean-*' trio (after csv and text). Three scripts in pure stdlib: parse.py (auto-detects apache-common/apache-combined/nginx-access/syslog/json-line formats, custom --regex with named groups, fallback generic timestamp+level extractor), errors.py (aggregate by level + time-bucket minute/hour/day, fingerprint normalization for message grouping, output as JSON/Markdown/CSV report), grep.py (pattern + --not-pattern + --level + --since/--until time window + -B/-A/-C context lines). Shared timestamp parser handles ISO 8601 with/without TZ/microseconds, apache common log, syslog. Safe-path policy and 0/1/2 exit-code contract. Zero third-party dependencies.
